text: Because ∇·B = 0 everywhere, the magnetic field can always be written in terms of a vector potential A as:
explanation: A divergence-free field is the curl of some vector potential, so B = ∇×A; this automatically guarantees ∇·B = 0 because the divergence of a curl vanishes. B = −∇φ describes the electrostatic field E, ∇·A is a scalar, and ∂A/∂t is only part of E in the time-dependent case.
